item.title: Ep 01: Why 80% of Online Sourdough Calculators Ruin Your Dough (The +3% Hidden Levain Water Error & Mass Conservation)
item.itunes:title: Why 80% of Online Sourdough Calculators Ruin Your Dough (The +3% Hidden Levain Water Error)
item.itunes:author: Julian Vance & SourdoughCalc Open Bread Lab
item.description: Why does a 75% hydration recipe from a food blog turn into soup while a commercial bakery's 75% loaf stands tall? Julian Vance and Clara Meyer audit 25 online sourdough calculators and reveal how ignoring starter flour and water decomposition hides +2.3% to +3.5% free water. Calculate your true hydration at https://sourdoughcalc.app.
item.content:encoded:
Calculate your true total dough hydration with zero starter mass distortion using the SourdoughCalc Master Hydration Engine and the Baker's Percentage & Levain Decomposition Calculator, or audit our empirical 2026 calculator benchmark study at SourdoughCalc Industry Statistics.

When we audited the top 25 free online sourdough calculators in 2026, 80% failed basic mass conservation. Instead of decomposing the inoculated levain (Mlev) into its constituent fermented flour (Flev) and water (Wlev) at its specific starter hydration (Hlev), naive calculators divide autolyse water strictly by unfermented main-bowl flour (Fmain). At a standard 20% inoculation of 100% hydration liquid starter, a recipe labeled "75% hydration" actually sits at 77.27% to 78.3% true total hydration.

Key Mathematical Equations Covered

  • Levain Flour Mass Decomposition: F_lev = M_lev / (1 + H_lev)
  • Levain Water Mass Decomposition: W_lev = M_lev - F_lev
  • True Total Dough Hydration: H_true = (W_main + W_lev) / (F_main + F_lev)
  • Exact Autolyse Water Solver: W_main = H_target * (F_main + F_lev) - W_lev

item.title: Ep 02: Saving Summer Bakes Above 78°F (The 4-Factor Desired Dough Temperature & 80 cal/g Crushed Ice Equation)
item.itunes:title: Saving Summer Bakes Above 78°F (4-Factor DDT & 80 cal/g Crushed Ice Math)
item.itunes:author: Julian Vance & SourdoughCalc Open Bread Lab
item.description: When summer kitchens climb past 78°F (25.5°C), wild yeast kinetics and protease enzymes go into overdrive. Learn the 4-Factor Desired Dough Temperature (DDT) equation and the 80 cal/g Latent Heat of Fusion ice-mass balance at https://sourdoughcalc.app/calculators/sourdough-desired-dough-temperature-calculator.
item.content:encoded:
Stop summer over-proofing before you mix a single gram of flour using the SourdoughCalc Master Formulation Suite and our 4-Factor Desired Dough Temperature (DDT) & Crushed Ice Calculator, backed by thermal telemetry at SourdoughCalc Industry Statistics.

When ambient kitchen temperatures climb past 78°F (25.5°C), sourdough fermentation accelerates exponentially along the Q10 ≈ 2.1 Van 't Hoff biological curve while endogenous protease enzymes shred gluten elasticity. Julian Vance and Clara Meyer derive the complete thermodynamic fix: the 4-Factor DDT Equation and the Latent Heat of Fusion Ice Substitution Formula (L_f = 80 cal/g) when your required water temperature drops below your cold tap limit.

Key Mathematical Equations Covered

  • 4-Factor DDT Required Water Temp: T_water = 4 * T_DDT - (T_room + T_flour + T_levain + Delta_T_friction)
  • Metric Crushed Ice Substitution (g, °C): M_ice = [M_water * (T_tap - T_req)] / (80 + T_tap)
  • Fahrenheit Equivalent (144 BTU/lb): M_ice = [M_water * (T_tap_F - T_req_F)] / [144 + (T_tap_F - 32)]

item.title: Ep 03: Why Waiting for Sourdough to "Double in Size" Destroys Your Gluten (3D Conical Bowl Frustum Math & Thermal Carryover)
item.itunes:title: Why Waiting for Sourdough to "Double in Size" Destroys Your Gluten (3D Frustum Math)
item.itunes:author: Julian Vance & SourdoughCalc Open Bread Lab
item.description: Waiting for dough to double its vertical height in a sloped mixing bowl actually triples or quadruples its volume! Plus why 30g aliquot jars fail whenever dough temp differs from room temp, and how Newton's Law of Cooling governs fridge carryover at https://sourdoughcalc.app/calculators/sourdough-bulk-fermentation-calculator.
item.content:encoded:
Calculate your exact target percentage rise and pull-time before cold retard using the SourdoughCalc Master Formulation Engine, the Bulk Fermentation & Thermal Carryover Calculator, and the Interactive Sourdough Crumb Doctor.

In Episode 03, Julian Vance and Clara Meyer dismantle the two most destructive myths in bulk fermentation: 3D Conical Bowl Height Illusion and Zero-Thermal-Inertia Aliquot Sampling. In a flared mixing bowl modeled as a conical frustum, a 100% volume doubling increases vertical height by only 34%. Furthermore, a 900g loaf placed into a 38°F (3.3°C) refrigerator retains fermentation momentum for 4 to 6 hours—meaning an 80°F dough must be shaped at 30% volumetric rise, whereas a 68°F dough requires 75% to 80% rise.

Key Mathematical Equations Covered

  • Conical Frustum Volume vs. Height: V(h) = (pi * h / 3) * (r_1^2 + r_1*r(h) + r(h)^2), r(h) = r_1 + h*tan(theta)
  • Newton's Law of Cooling in Cold Retard: T_core(t) = T_fridge + (T_initial - T_fridge) * exp(-t / tau)
  • Temperature-Compensated Target Rise: 80°F → 30% rise | 75°F → 50% rise | 70°F → 75% rise

item.title: Ep 04: King Arthur 12.7% vs. European T55 & Whole Rye Pentosans (Calculating Your Flour Blend's True Absorption Ceiling)
item.itunes:title: King Arthur 12.7% vs. European T55 & Rye Pentosans (Flour Absorption Ceilings)
item.itunes:author: Julian Vance & SourdoughCalc Open Bread Lab
item.description: Why does an 80% hydration American Tartine recipe turn French T55 or German Type 550 flour into soup? Discover the 0.86 conversion factor between EU Dry-Basis protein and US 14%-Moisture-Basis protein, plus how rye pentosans and spelt gliadins shift your hydration ceiling at https://sourdoughcalc.app.
item.content:encoded:
Calculate the exact maximum water absorption ceiling for any custom blend of North American bread flour, European T55/T65, Tipo 00, whole wheat, spelt, or rye using the SourdoughCalc Master Hydration & Flour Blend Solver, the Multi-Flour Baker's Percentage Calculator, and our global flour dataset at SourdoughCalc Industry Statistics.

European laboratories report flour protein on a 0% Dry Matter Basis while North American mills (AACC standard) report on a 14% Moisture Basis—meaning a European flour labeled 11.5% protein is actually 9.89% protein on the American scale! Julian Vance and Clara Meyer explain Chopin Alveograph W-values, damaged starch absorption, rye arabinoxylan pentosans (which bind 8x their weight in water), and spelt gliadin extensibility.

Key Mathematical Equations Covered

  • EU Dry-Basis to US 14% Moisture-Basis Protein: P_14% = 0.86 * P_dry
  • Composite Multi-Flour Absorption Ceiling: H_max = H_base + alpha_pro * (P_eff - 11.5) + sum(f_i * Delta_H_i)
  • Grain Absorption Modifiers: Whole Wheat +0.12 g/g | Whole Rye Pentosans +0.25 g/g | Spelt -0.08 g/g

item.title: Ep 05: Converting Any Commercial Yeast Recipe to Sourdough (50% Lievito Madre to 125% Liquid Levain) & Discard Acid Neutralization Chemistry
item.itunes:title: Converting Commercial Yeast to Sourdough & Zero-Waste Discard Acid Chemistry
item.itunes:author: Julian Vance & SourdoughCalc Open Bread Lab
item.description: Replace the broken "1 packet of yeast = 100g starter" rule with exact mass-conservation equations across 50% stiff Lievito Madre to 125% liquid levain. Plus the 0.85g per 100g sodium bicarbonate stoichiometry for zero-waste sourdough discard at https://sourdoughcalc.app/calculators/sourdough-discard-calculator.
item.content:encoded:
Convert any commercial yeast bread, pizza, or enriched brioche recipe to natural levain—or reformulate any pastry around leftover discard—using the SourdoughCalc Master Formulation Engine, the Commercial Yeast-to-Sourdough Converter, and the Zero-Waste Sourdough Discard & Acid Neutralization Calculator.

Why do blog rules telling you to "swap 1 packet (7g) of yeast for 100g starter" wreck enriched doughs and small batches? Julian Vance and Clara Meyer present the unified mass-conservation equations across 50% stiff Lievito Madre to 125% liquid levain, explain why high-sugar/high-butter brioche demands stiff starter to overcome osmotic stress, and derive the exact sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) stoichiometry (0.85g per 100g discard) to neutralize lactic and acetic acids in discard pancakes, waffles, and muffins.

Key Mathematical Equations Covered

  • Commercial Yeast Equivalency: M_IDY = 0.80 * M_ADY = 0.333 * M_fresh
  • Sourdough Mass-Preserving Substitution: F_new = F_recipe - M_lev / (1 + H_lev), W_new = W_recipe - M_lev * [H_lev / (1 + H_lev)]
  • Discard Acid Neutralization Stoichiometry: M_NaHCO3_bonus = 0.0085 * M_discard (at pH 3.9–4.1, TTA 12 mL)
